recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future financial cardinality changes should be made through current resource-specific trackers, not by using FHIR-11408 to make all current financial-resource root elements optional.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FM issue FHIR-11408 asked to reduce financial resource root attribute cardinalities to optional because supporting parties might not know required values, with the recorded resolution to reduce all cardinalities to 0..? on root elements.
initial_application: Two 2016 commits, 37303c8e87f010b309f155116763f10165ef6d3f and 7fc33d1f033151db47e1313bc21a0721969f873b, explicitly applied Tracker #11408 across the financial spreadsheets. Parsing the old spreadsheet XML before and after shows required direct children on the listed resources were reduced so no direct children remained required after the second commit.
additional_context: The current build uses active StructureDefinition XML for Claim, ClaimResponse, CoverageEligibilityRequest, CoverageEligibilityResponse, EnrollmentRequest, EnrollmentResponse, ExplanationOfBenefit, PaymentNotice, PaymentReconciliation, and VisionPrescription. EligibilityRequest/EligibilityResponse are now mapped to CoverageEligibilityRequest/CoverageEligibilityResponse, while ProcessRequest/ProcessResponse are not active current resources. Later Published/Persuasive issues such as FHIR-19457, FHIR-19463, FHIR-19490, FHIR-19491, FHIR-19493, FHIR-19494, FHIR-19496, FHIR-17986, and FHIR-18029 reworked or reintroduced specific required fields.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reapplying the old DSTU2 blanket optionality rule to the current R6 source would undo later work-group decisions rather than fix a missed FHIR-11408 change.
